ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is capacitor C1 and the right side is capacitor C2; the lower ends of the two capacitors have already been connected into a common node by the bottom wire. Their upper ends are respectively connected to the two sides of the top wire, with an ideal switch S in the middle, labeled as closing at t = 0. The figure also shows the direction of the loop current i(t). Reasoning: The problem gives that C1 has been charged to 12 V before the switch closes. After switch S closes at t = 0, the upper nodes of C1 and C2 are shorted by the ideal switch, while the lower nodes are originally a common node, so the two ideal capacitors must immediately have the same terminal voltage. If an ideal capacitor voltage changes instantaneously, from i = C dv/dt it can be known that the corresponding current cannot be an ordinary finite current, and can only be concentrated in a Dirac impulse at t = 0; when t ≠ 0 there is no ordinary current in a continuous path. Therefore i(t) is an impulse function.

method.method_draft: After describing the image topology, use the text fact that C1 is initially at 12 V before the ideal switch closes. Since this requires an instantaneous change in at least one ideal capacitor voltage, i(t)=C dv/dt cannot be an ordinary finite current; it is nonzero only as a Dirac impulse at t=0 and zero otherwise. Therefore the current for all time is an impulse function.
